title: Pune home-services marketplace beat cold-start by faking liquidity in one pincode cluster: response rate 11% → 73%, then cloned it
content: SITUATION: A Pune home-services marketplace (electricians, plumbers, AC repair) was stuck in classic chicken-and-egg. It got ~40 customer requests/day but only 11% drew any provider response, because just 60 verified pros were scattered thin across all of Pune — nobody was ever close enough to bother. Acquisition bled ₹4.2L/month on Meta at a ₹380 CAC, fill time averaged 6 hours, and repeat sat at 18% — paid customers churned after one bad wait. ACTION: We killed city-wide and concentrated supply into 4 adjacent pincodes (Kothrud–Bavdhan), onboarding 35 pros there via Justdial sourcing plus area WhatsApp electrician/plumber groups. To fake liquidity on the scarce supply side, we paid a ₹150 'show-up guarantee' per accepted job for the first 8 weeks — a deliberate subsidy, not the unit economics. Demand was geo-fenced on Meta and Google to those pincodes only, WhatsApp click-to-chat as the single CTA, and we seeded Instagram reviews from the first 120 real jobs. OUTCOME over 90 days: response rate jumped 11% → 73%, fill time dropped 6 hours → 38 minutes, the tighter funnel cut CAC ₹380 → ₹210, and repeat hit 34%. The cluster did 900 jobs/month at ~₹230 take; net of the tapering subsidy, contribution settled near ₹95/job — positive without the guarantee. Only then did we clone the playbook to Hinjewadi. LESSON below.
lesson: Marketplace liquidity is geographic, never aggregate — 60 pros across a city is zero density; 35 in four pincodes is a market. Pick the densest cluster, subsidize the scarce side hard enough to fake liquidity, then watch one number: contribution per job WITHOUT the subsidy. Do not clone to the next cluster until that number is positive on its own — otherwise you are just paying to scale a loss, pincode by pincode.
